This paper introduces the general steps of data acquisition in anaesthesia and summarizes some data acquisition systems. It also introduces some applications of the burgeoning field of artificial intelligence (AI) to data acquisition, illustrating how AI techniques may be used to advantage to assist the anaesthesiologist in monitoring and interpreting such data.

articleTitle: An Optimization Tool for Displacing Photovoltaic Arrays in Polygonal Areas
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the problem of optimally designing the layout of a given number of photovoltaic arrays on a flat polygonal surface, in order to maximize a suitable objective function, e.g., the total generated energy. This means finding their optimal position, azimuth and tilt. The considered problem becomes non-trivial when considering effects such as irradiance variability and self-shadowing. We first provide a description of the system model and the associated optimization problem, showing how the resulting formulation presents non-convexities. Then, we provide a tight parametrized convex relaxation, which is computationally tractable and for which optimality conditions hold. We provide numerical simulations using realistic data, showing how the proposed methodology yields near-optimal solutions in lower computational time with respect to the traditional global resolution approach.

articleTitle: ANN Based Energy Management System for V2X - EV aggregator in cold climate application
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: This paper presents the development of an energy management system (EMS) dedicated to an aggregator for energy dispatch among a fleet of electric vehicles (EVs). This EMS main objective is to manage the total energy demand from plugged-in EVs to reduce the overall load on the grid, considering the effects of cold temperatures and human habits on the total demand of energy. The approach used to achieve this objective is training an artificial neural network (ANN) using Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LMA). The training dataset is based on climate data, on actual energy consumption in Quebec (Canada), and on real energy and power consumption from an EV charging station that can accept up to 30 vehicles. The results show that the LMA was effective to train three specialized EMS to predict accurate reference power for charging and discharging EVs in summer and winter with a minimal mean square error and maximal R-squared.

articleTitle: Quantitative comparison between male and female soccer players motor performance
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: In recent years, the interest in women's soccer has risen considerably. Has thus became clear the need to develop specific training programs to improve physical performance of young female players. The aim of the study is to quantitatively compare male and female soccer players motor performance, to develop training programs specific for female players. One hundred-thirty-one male athletes and eighty female athletes were assessed at the same timepoint (T0) by means of Riablo™ medical device (CoRehab, Rovereto (TN), Italy). The tests included were a stability test (ST) (two-leg and one-leg), countermovement jump test (CMJ) (two-leg and oneleg), plyometric jumps (PJ), parkour test (PK) (one-leg) and quick feet test (QF). The comparisons were performed throught the unpaired samples t-test (p<0.003 (0.05/18) after a Bonferroni correction). The results showed that the female group obtained better results in the ST. The CMJ and PK performance, instead, are higher in the male group rather than in the female one. For the PJ and the QF test, instead, no significant differences are shown. This study has tried to find out a test battery reliable for the comparison between male and female motor performance. As the differences in the performance are in the ST, CMJ and PK tests, these three tests are fundamental to assess the dissimilarities between sexes. Anyway, further studies should analyze also the technical and tactical differences to develop more specific training programs.

articleTitle: Direct and Inverse Neural Modelling of Buildings HVAC Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: The present paper describes an approach to develop a neural network model approach to characterize the thermal and electrical relationship in a climatized building. The approach is fundamental for the inclusion of such building in an grid with demand-response strategy, such as a micro-grid or a renewable energy community. The approach is based on the simulation of different buildings with variable boundary conditions in the EnergyPlus environment. This simulation is used to create a database of electrical and thermal profiles, which is then used to create direct (electrical to thermal) and inverse (thermal to electrical) models of the building. Both models were validated against test data to assess the accuracy of their predictions.

articleTitle: Design of an Automated Flotation Cell for Laboratory Operations Using Model-Based System Engineering
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: Automation in flotation cells has become an increasingly popular topic in the mineral processing industry due to its ability to increase efficiency and reduce operational costs. This paper discusses the design and implementation of an automated flotation cell system for a mineral processing plant. The system utilizes advanced control algorithms and sensors to optimize the flotation process, resulting in improved product quality and reduced energy consumption. This manuscript outlines the first stage in the creation and development of an automated flotation cell for use in educational and research settings, using model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and systems modeling language (SysML) via the CESAM modeling and architecting framework. Our case study employs this method to construct and demonstrate an operational perspective layout of the flotation cell's initial design phase. Moreover, the potential for the automation of flotation cells is highlighted as a promising avenue for improving sustainability and revolutionizing the mineral processing industry.

articleTitle: Using machine learning to advance computational efficiency in stochastic hosting capacity evaluations
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: Assessment of distribution networks' hosting capacity (HC) is critical for optimal integration and utilization of distributed energy resources (DERs). DERs have various uncertainties which must be captured for accurate HC assessment. Stochastic hosting capacity (SHC) methods allow comprehensive and accurate HC analysis given their ability to simulate a wide range of input scenarios. However, due to the need of load flow assessment for each input scenario, SHC methods have extensive computational requirements. Various computational efficiency improvements in SHC analysis have been proposed but the use of machine learning (ML) in such applications is still limited. This paper presents an efficient ML-driven SHC (SHC-ML) method based on linear regression. The proposed method utilizes a limited scenario set to train an ML model that accurately and efficiently predicts the voltage impact of a comprehensive, larger input scenario set. This approach significantly reduces the number of load flow computations in the SHC assessment. The proposed method is demonstrated on three low-voltage distribution feeders with rooftop photovoltaic systems. The results show that a significantly reduced subset as low as 0.003<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>of the standard SHC scenario set can sufficiently train an SHC-ML model to accurately predict voltage impacts given DER penetration scenarios. The reduction in the conducted load flow assessments improves the computational efficiency of the SHC analysis by a factor of up to 17, with high accuracy (>99<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). The results have significant implications for the optimal integration and utilization of DERs.

articleTitle: Development of Programmable Logic Controller Emulator With QEMU
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: It is crucial to ensure the security of programmable logic controllers (PLCs), as any compromise of these devices can have a significant impact on the safety and stability of the industrial process. An exploited vulnerability could affect production, damage the plant, and potentially put people at risk. To make them secure, various forms of third-party testing can be performed. However, because the firmware and hardware used in most PLCs is proprietary, firmware testing is difficult. The firmware code may be encrypted, compressed, and/or obfuscated. Even if the firmware is acquired, it is unlikely to run without the PLC because it depends too much on the hardware, which means testing is limited by the availability and processing speed of the PLC. To solve this problem, emulation could be used to speed up testing, but to properly emulate the behavior of the hardware, knowledge of peripheral device communication is required. In this work, we present a method to obtain the necessary information to emulate a proprietary PLC and run its firmware in an emulator, which to our knowledge has not been done before. We acquired the bootloader and firmware for a Siemens S7-1200 PLC and modeled the communication between the firmware and the peripheral devices using reverse engineering methods. The models were then implemented in the QEMU emulator. The end result is a partial emulation of the PLC, demonstrating that emulation of even a proprietary PLC is possible. The emulation shows the potential for future integration with a dynamic testing tool.

articleTitle: Inertial-based Six-Minute Walking Test Assessment in Post-Covid Patients: Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: The 6MWT is sub-maximal test used by clinicians to assess functional exercise capacity in patients with various conditions. Its main outcome is the distance covered by the patient over the test duration, which is often used either to measure patient's functional status and for pre/post-treatment comparisons. The instrumented version of the 6MWT (i.e. i6MWT), based on the application of wearable-inertial devices, allows for the obtainment of other meaningful parameters, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of gait. The aim of this study was to apply the i6MWT to assess the effects of a two-stage rehabilitation treatment for patients reporting disabling motor and respiratory symptoms after Covid-19 infection. Thirteen post-Covid patients were assessed via the i6MWT in three sessions (T0, hospital admittance; T1, discharge time; T2, after tele-rehabilitation). So far, the data retrieved from the 7 patients who completed the full rehabilitative path were considered, showing an increasing trend for all the assessed gait parameters between the considered time points. The preliminary results thus suggest that the proposed rehabilitative intervention could have positive effects on the recovery of functional exercise capacity in post-Covid patients.

articleTitle: Exploring the suitability of a Digital twin- and eXtended Reality-based telepresence platform for a collaborative robotics training scenario over next-generation mobile networks
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: This paper explores the application of Digital Twins (DTs) and eXtended Reality (XR) in the context of Industry 4.0, and investigates new ways in which these technologies can be used in remote assistance/training scenarios involving Collaborative Robots (CRs). The study builds upon a previous work that examined the suitability of a novel DT/XR-based telepresence platform for CR programming in terms of network capabilities. The present work addresses some of the limitations of the previous study in the context of a new use case, integrating human pose estimation and object tracking to enhance the DT functionalities of the platform, and testing it in a riveting task scenario. The results in terms of bandwidth and latencies obtained in a laboratory setup emulating 6G performance show the potential of DTs and XR in supporting the collaboration of distant human operators and CRs over future mobile networks, paving the way for the development of new services for next-generation industry.

articleTitle: Benefits of an Advanced AC OPF Model in the Croatian Transmission Network
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: Modern transmission systems operation and planing problems involve computationally difficult optimizations. Transmission system operators forecast, monitor and manage power flows to ensure that the system always operates within permitted limits. This paper develops an AC Optimal Power Flow (AC OPF) algorithm intended to enhance numerical efficiency for commonly occurring cases in real-world transmission system networks. These systems include discrete devices, e.g. controllable transformer tap, generator automatic voltage control and variable shunt reactor (VSR), whose operational models are too computationally demanding for general nonlinear optimization. The developed algorithm divides the computational burden in two parts. The first part solves AC OPF with computationally demanding binary variables fixed to the initial power flow state, while the second part tries to find a better solution for fixed variables using more tractable AC OPF approximation. The efficiency of the approach is demonstrated on the Croatian transmission network and real operating data. The optimization succeeds to satisfy the initially exceeded operating constraints. Results also indicate that the direct approach that solves for all variables simultaneously using the exact nonlinear AC OPF model is computationally intractable for the considered cases.

articleTitle: Disentangling the Link between Telemedicine and Organization: Evidence from Case Studies
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: In the last decade, healthcare systems have undergone rapid transformations mainly enabled by technological innovations under the Industry 4.0 paradigm. Telemedicine is considered one of the key technological innovations to cope with contemporary health challenges, such as the accessibility of care pathways and related global health inclusion. However, despite its potential benefits and the acceleration of its use in the Covid-19 pandemic, the diffusion of telemedicine services is jeopardized across Europe, yet. Adopting a multiple case study approach, this paper explores how healthcare organizations have implemented telemedicine projects. This research focuses on Southern Italy, where the diffusion of telemedicine appears to be limited compared to other European and Italian regions. The paper aims to shed light on the implemented managerial actions for change and the role of the actors involved in telemedicine services in a disadvantaged territorial context.

articleTitle: Power Theory Based Dimensionality Reduction for Fault Detection and Identification in Power Electronics
publicationTitle: IEEE EUROCON 2023 - 20th International Conference on Smart Technologies
abstract: This paper presents a new approach in fault detection and identification (FDI) applications using power definitions (PD) based on Characteristic Current Components (CCC) for features extraction (FE) purposes. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based methods rely on FE methods to obtain information from time series data. FE is often achieved using Wavelet (Packet-) or Fourier Series decomposition. Due to high model test complexity, these methods may not be ideal for real-time FDI in large scale inverter applications such as Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC). Thus, this paper proposes the use of PD in order to reduce the dimension of the FE vectors to only few scalar active and non-active power components. In this article four power components according the CCC are utilised that result from FFT-transformed current and voltage (I/U) signals. This new approach of dimensionality reduction can effectively reduce classification model test time while not relying on problem-specific optimisations or expert knowledge. The proposed dimensionality reduction performance is compared experimentally by training various types of classification algorithms with either FFT-based or FFT-based FE with PD-based dimensionality reduction (PD-FE) using data from open-circuit faults (OCF) occurring in an MMC.
